Extract bouts of illness from a flusurvey data table

Source: R/bouts.r
bouts_of_illness.Rd

Extract bouts of illness from a flusurvey data table

Usage

bouts_of_illness(
  x,
  symptomatic.only = TRUE,
  as.data.frame = TRUE,
  start.date = c("earliest", "last"),
  missing.start = c("first.report", "missing"),
  inverted.dates = c("keep", "clear", "reset.end"),
  daily.flags = c("none", "carry.forward", "bout", "report"),
  precedence = c("dates", "continuation", "report.date"),
  unresolved = c("fill", "missing"),
  chronic = c("none", "duration"),
  chronic.days = NULL
)

Arguments

x

the data to extract bouts from

symptomatic.only

whether to only include symptomatic periods

as.data.frame

currently has no effect

start.date

which reported start date to use for a bout: the "earliest" one reported (the default, because the last reported date can fall after a report that already gives symptoms of the bout), or the "last" one

missing.start

what to use as start date if none was reported for a bout: the date of its "first.report", or "missing"

inverted.dates

what to do if the end date is before the start date: "keep" both, set both to "clear" (missing), or "reset.end" to the last report date of the bout

daily.flags

how to assign the case-definition flags set by aggregate_symptoms to the days of a bout. "none" returns one row per bout. The other values return one row per day, in the column day, from symptoms.start.date to symptoms.end.date. "carry.forward" takes the flags from the last report on or before the day. "bout" gives every day the flags of the bout. "report" sets flags only on days with a report. Missing or inverted selected intervals are not expanded.

precedence

how a report joins the previous bout. A report answered "no" always starts a new bout. Otherwise, with "dates", a report whose start date is after the previous end date starts a new bout, even if it is answered "yes". With "continuation", a report answered "yes" stays in the bout whatever its dates. With "report.date", a report whose start date is after the previous report date starts a new bout.

unresolved

what to do with a bout with no reported end date: "fill" its end with the last report date, or leave it "missing"

chronic

Rule for chronic-only reports: "none" applies no rule; "duration" excludes symptomatic reports with a valid interval longer than chronic.days days from bout reconstruction. Duration alone does not establish that symptoms are chronic.

chronic.days

Number of days beyond which a report is excluded when chronic = "duration".

Value

a data table of bouts of illness, or of their days

Details

The flags of a bout (those of the case definitions in aggregate_symptoms) are computed from the symptoms of all its reports together: a bout meets the symptom-based ILI definition if its reports jointly have the symptoms and a sudden onset, even if no single report does. The flags describe the bout and do not say that the symptoms were present together on one day. The days of illness that the reports establish, and which dates are reported and which only the date of a report, are in bout_evidence.

Author

seb

Examples

dt <- extract_data(simulated_data, years = 2013:2014)
#> Warning: The contact and symptom surveys are joined by report date, which pairs each symptom report with the latest earlier contact report however long before it was filed, and (with 'unsuccessful.join') drops symptom reports that have none. To link contacts to illness, extract them separately and use contact_illness().
#> Warning: The contact and symptom surveys are joined by report date, which pairs each symptom report with the latest earlier contact report however long before it was filed, and (with 'unsuccessful.join') drops symptom reports that have none. To link contacts to illness, extract them separately and use contact_illness().
